key_insight: Adding reaction kinetics to alloy-screening changes the best catalyst from Pt-rich, single-site-optimized compositions to a compositionally diverse multicomponent nanoparticle with better hydrogen evolution performance.
engineering_relevance: The workflow provides a practical way to search vast alloy composition spaces for more effective and cost-aware HER catalysts by combining machine learning, thermodynamics, and kinetic simulation.
method: Machine-learning models predicted adsorption energetics for 85-atom nanoparticle models across a nine-element alloy space.
Monte Carlo sampling generated thermodynamically plausible nanoparticle configurations for screening.
Kinetic Monte Carlo simulation ranked candidates by dynamic reaction behavior rather than static adsorption energy alone.
evidence_signal: Among the evaluated candidates, static optimization favored Pt-rich low-component alloys, while kMC-based optimization identified Au33Co20Cu6Pd26 as the top performer and revealed site-specific adsorption, migration, and desorption steps.
watch_item: Results depend on model accuracy, finite nanoparticle size, and the specific reaction-network assumptions used in the kMC pathway analysis.
paper_title: Dynamic Kinetic Evaluation Favors Compositionally Diverse Multicomponent Alloy Nanoparticles for Hydrogen Evolution
